newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-CANADIAN'S WITHDRAWAL TWISTS KNIFE FOR CHEN.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-CANADIAN'S WITHDRAWAL TWISTS KNIFE FOR CHEN.

text.p: Canadian champion Susan Humphreys withdrew from the world figure skating championships with a foot ailment on Saturday, adding a new twist to former champion Chen Lu's failure to qualify.
Humphreys pulled out with an infection caused by an abscess on her left ankle a day after qualifying as one of the 24 for Saturday's final.
Her success on Friday pushed Chen down to 25th place in the short programme, one spot outside the final and one place away from earning China a place in next year's Olympic and world championships.
Ironically, it was a foot injury that cost Chen four months of skating and caused her form to dip so far after winning two years ago and finishing second last year.

To add to the irony, Humphreys was the final skater to perform on Friday, at a point when Chen was 23rd out of 29. The Canadian missed her first two jumps and had she missed the third she would probably not have qualified.
But she landed it and finished 21st. Her scores scrambled the positions of the lower-placed skaters so that Chen dropped two places to 25th.
Humphreys's withdrawal also cost Canada their automatic qualifying spot for next winter's Olympics.
Chen and Humphreys will now both have to skate in a special event in Vienna to earn places for their countries in the Games.
There is no provision in the rules to restore Chen to the final 24 after the withdrawal of another skater.
